transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you for taking the time to see me. 

Um, I guess the main thing that pushed me to come in is... well, I process insurance claims for work, and I just sort of keep getting up from my workstation during the day? Like, even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, I end up leaving my desk. 

It's probably not the worst thing in the world, but I really want to do a good job at work, and I feel a little bad that I can't just sit there and power through like everyone else seems to do. Does that make sense? I just wanted to see if maybe there was a way to get better at it, if that's the sort of thing you can help with?
When you get up from your desk, do you usually feel physically restless, like you just can’t stay seated?

Um, I wouldn't say it's like a severe physical thing where I absolutely can't stay seated? I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. It's more just... well, like during trainings or those longer team meetings we have, I try really hard to look focused and be respectful of whoever is speaking. But I guess I'm usually bouncing my leg a lot, or maybe clicking my pen, or just sort of shifting around in my chair. 

I always try to keep it really subtle so I'm not being disruptive to the rest of the team, I promise. It's just a little bit of nervous energy, I think? Does that answer your question, or did you mean something else?
When you get up from your desk, is it usually because you feel you need to check or redo something to make sure nothing was missed?

Oh, no, it's not really like that. I don't think I'm getting up to double-check my work or anything. I mean, I try to be really careful with the claims the first time through so I don't have to redo them. 

When I get up, it's usually just... I don't know, maybe to grab a coffee, or I'll just sort of wander over to the printer even if I didn't print anything. It's just a quick break, really. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm slacking off, because I do care about getting everything done right. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Since you were a child, have you often had trouble paying attention or staying focused, even when you wanted to?

Um, I guess so? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad student or anything, because I really did try my best to be good. But, yeah, looking back, this kind of thing isn't exactly brand new for me. 

Like, in elementary school, my teachers were always really nice and they'd write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, which was sweet of them. But they would also usually mention that I... well, that I lost my worksheets sometimes, or maybe missed some of the instructions when they were talking. And I guess I needed a few extra reminders to finish my classwork compared to the other kids. 

It wasn't that I was trying to be defiant or anything, I promise. I just sort of... drifted off, I guess? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a problem child. Does that make sense for what you're asking?
When you have trouble focusing, is it usually because your mind is caught up in worrying?

Oh, um, no, I wouldn't say it's because I'm worrying. I mean, I care about doing a good job with the claims, so I might stress a tiny bit if I get behind, but it's not like I'm sitting there caught up in anxious thoughts or anything. I don't want you to think I'm, like, a super nervous person who can't handle things. 

It's usually more just... blanking out, I guess? Like, I'll be reading through a file, and suddenly I realize I've just been thinking about what I need to pick up at the grocery store, or maybe a movie I watched the night before. It's just random stuff, not really worries. I always try my best to keep my personal thoughts out of my work time, I promise. Does that answer your question okay?
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks, like figuring out the steps or keeping materials in order?

Um, well, I really do try my best to keep everything neat. I know how important it is to stay on top of things and be professional. But... I guess lately, since my caseload got a bit bigger, it's been kind of an adjustment. 

I hate to admit it, because I really want to do a good job, but my claim folders and my little reminder notes have sort of ended up all over the place on my desk. And my email flags are a bit scattered, too. Sometimes I just sit down and I have a really hard time figuring out which policy review I should tackle first when there's so much in front of me. 

I'm definitely working on finding a better system, though, I promise. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent or like a complete mess... is it normal to struggle with that kind of thing when work gets busy?
Do you often feel anxious or on edge, even when there isn’t a specific reason?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't walk around feeling on edge or anything like that. I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? 

I guess sometimes if I'm running late or if a supervisor asks for an update on a file I haven't finished, I might feel a little tense for a second, but that's just because I want to make sure I'm meeting expectations. It's never just out of nowhere, and it goes away as soon as I get the work done. I definitely wouldn't say I'm an anxious person overall. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for?
